reason: Candidate is a distinct micro_skill for DOM event listener attachment/removal via selection.on(). It has semantic identity separate from peer candidates (custom event dispatch, zoom event registration, pointer extraction) and existing skills (prefetch, future callbacks). No existing skill covers the core capability of managing generic DOM event listeners on selections. Supported by API index evidence.

skill.name: Event listener management
skill.description: Add, remove, or manage event listeners on DOM selections using selection.on(). Use when you need to attach or detach event handlers to interactive elements.
skill.skill_body:
Use selection.on(type, listener) to add an event listener or selection.on(type, null) to remove it. The listener callback receives the event object and the datum associated with the element.

## Objective

Attach or detach event handlers to DOM selections
## Applicable Signals

- Element selection is available
- Event type is native DOM event (click, mouseover, etc.)
- Callback logic is defined

## Contraindications

- Event is synthetic or programmatically dispatched; use selection.dispatch instead
- Custom event dispatch is required

## Workflow Steps

- Select the target DOM element(s)
- Define the event type (e.g., 'click', 'mouseover')
- Define the listener callback function
- Call selection.on(type, listener) to attach or selection.on(type, null) to remove

## Constraints

- Event type must be a valid DOM event name
- Listener must be a function or null (to remove)

## Cautions

- Removing a listener requires the exact same function reference
- Multiple listeners on the same event type will all fire

## Output Contract

- Event listener is registered or removed; subsequent user interaction on the element triggers the callback with the event object and associated datum as arguments.
